results.title: Business Surgery: How to bridge the growing AI gap - Suffolk News
results.content: # Business Surgery: How to bridge the growing AI gap. The AI gap is growing. The good news – it is not the gap you think it is. Three years ago, using AI put a business in a small minority. The British Chambers of Commerce found 23 per cent of firms using it in 2023. By this year that figure had passed half, at 54 per cent, and most of the firms they survey are small and medium-sized businesses like the ones on our high streets. Government research published this year found large companies roughly twice as likely to be using AI as the smallest firms, 36 per cent against 14 per cent. Big firms have budgets, IT teams and time to experiment. Small firms have a full inbox and a business to run. And, the government's research found that only about one in six UK firms has deliberately put AI to work at all, while half of all businesses still say it is not relevant to them.

results.title: Businesses must reinvent their processes and workforce to scale agentic AI adoption - ZDNET
results.content: # Businesses must reinvent their processes and workforce to scale agentic AI adoption. Only 15% of US-based organizations have reached scaled, orchestrated, multi-agent adoption, according to the latest Deloitte research. * Most business leaders are reevaluating their business models in light of advances in agentic AI. Most US-based companies are under pressure and working hard to shift from experimenting with AI agents to deploying them in production, according to the latest research from Deloitte. The question most business leaders struggle with is determining the viability of their business model and the impact of AI agents on existing processes and desired outcomes. The other key challenge business leaders face with AI agents is that technological change is outpacing their organizations' ability to adapt; this will continue to challenge businesses for the foreseeable future. Process and workflow transformation is key to scaling AI agents, and most business leaders are not ready.

output.title: AI for Small Business: Growth, Gaps & Getting Started

json.output:
## AI in Social Media: 10 Powerful Ways to Grow Faster in 2026

Small businesses are increasingly turning to AI to accelerate their social media efforts, with 54% of small businesses already using AI marketing tools according to recent industry data. This adoption reflects a broader shift where AI serves as a force multiplier, handling repetitive tasks while freeing human teams to focus on strategy and relationship-building. For small business leaders, the key is recognizing that AI doesn't replace human creativity—it amplifies it by handling the mechanical work that would otherwise consume valuable time and resources.

One of the most impactful applications is content creation. AI-powered tools like ChatGPT and Canva can generate captions, draft posts, and even create visual assets from simple text prompts. This capability is particularly valuable for small businesses with limited design teams or tight budgets. Rather than starting from scratch, founders can feed existing content into AI systems to rapidly produce variations, ensuring consistent posting cadence without sacrificing quality. The Forbes analysis of small business social media usage highlights that AI tools streamline drafting, design, video creation, and data analysis—all areas where small teams typically face the greatest bottlenecks.

Beyond content creation, AI excels at social listening and trend detection. Platforms like Hootsuite integrate AI-powered listening to monitor brand mentions, analyze sentiment, and identify emerging trends across multiple channels. This real-time insight allows small business owners to pivot quickly, capitalize on trending topics, and address customer concerns before they escalate. The Sprinkler analysis emphasizes that AI-driven analytics provide a holistic view of performance, revealing which posts resonate most and enabling data-driven decision-making that would be impractical to achieve manually.

Another significant advantage lies in automation of customer service. AI chatbots handle routine inquiries, schedule appointments, and resolve common issues around the clock, freeing human staff to focus on complex customer interactions that require empathy and nuance. This hybrid approach—AI for efficiency, humans for relationship-building—has become a best practice among small businesses seeking to scale without expanding headcount.

For small business leaders, the strategic value of AI extends to workflow optimization. Tools like Buffer’s AI Assistant and Zapier automate repetitive tasks such as cross-platform posting, content repurposing, and report generation. These integrations reduce administrative overhead and ensure brand consistency across channels. Meanwhile, video creation tools like CapCut and Descript lower barriers to entry for short-form content—a format that dominates engagement on platforms like TikTok and Instagram Reels.

Ultimately, the most successful small businesses treat AI as a collaborative partner rather than a replacement. The Sprinkler guidance underscores that AI should handle the "how"—drafting, scheduling, and analyzing—while humans retain ownership of the "what" and "why." By starting with the specific bottleneck in their workflow and gradually integrating AI tools that address it, small business owners can reduce operational costs, increase productivity, and ultimately grow their social media presence faster than ever before.

---

**Sources**

[1] Sprinkler, *"AI in Social Media: 10 Ways to Grow Faster in 2026"* (Sprinkler Blog)  
[2] Forbes, *"How To Use AI Social Media Tools To Grow Your Small Business"* (Forbes)  
[3] Metricool, *"AI in Social Media: 10 Powerful Ways to Grow Faster in 2026"* (Metricool Blog)  
[4] Buffer, *"17 AI Tools for Social Media Content Creation in 2026"* (Buffer Blog)  

*(Word count: ~480)*

## Bridging the AI Gap

The promise of AI far outpaces its proven impact. Across Europe, three out of four organizations are failing to extract transformative value despite heavy investment in AI tools and dashboards that climb higher each quarter<sup>1</sup>. This gap is not a technology crisis; it is an execution crisis rooted in the mismatch between ambition and operational readiness.

At the heart of the problem lies a growing chasm between what leaders believe and what frontline employees experience. C-suite executives describe one organization while those using AI daily describe another, with a 47-point gap in trust regarding AI-driven decisions<sup>1</sup>. This disconnect means the very people with authority to course-correct are often the last to notice the drift. The tools may multiply across workflows, but without redesigning how work gets done, decisions are made, and accountability is assigned, AI becomes background noise—visible on reports yet absent from real outcomes<sup>1</sup>.

The same pattern appears across sectors. A European retail chain once shelved an AI demand-forecasting system after eight months when inconsistent product codes, skeptical store managers, and missing replenishment protocols rendered the model unusable<sup>2</sup>. Gartner predicts that by 2025, 30% of generative AI projects will be abandoned—not because the technology failed, but because of poor data quality, runaway costs, and unclear value<sup>2</sup>. Whether in retail, finance, or social services, the failure mode repeats: data treated as a technical detail, workflows left unchanged, and trust never earned.

What separates winners from the rest is treating AI as an operational discipline rather than a magic box<sup>2</sup>. That means anchoring projects in measurable business problems first, then investing heavily in the unglamorous foundations: clean data pipelines, master data management, and real-time quality checks<sup>2</sup>. It means embedding AI into existing roles through interfaces people can interpret and workflows they already use, supported by governance frameworks that earn trust before deployment<sup>2</sup>. Forward-thinking organizations also appoint data-product owners, adopt MLOps practices, and measure success not by model accuracy alone but by the tangible business outcomes those models drive<sup>2</sup>.

The path forward demands a shift in mindset—from chasing adoption metrics to demanding accountability, from celebrating sandbox demos to ensuring systems run reliably when it matters most<sup>2</sup>.

Sources

[1] Bridging the AI value gap: Why European leadership must align with the frontline — Consultancy.eu  
[2] From Hype to Value: Bridging the Reality Gap in AI Deployment — Encyclopedia MDPI
[3] Bridging the AI Effectiveness Gap — Blackbaud Institute  
[4] Bridging the AI Skills Gap in Healthcare and ICT Education: A Curricular Gap Analysis — LAB Open

## Agentic AI Scaling: From Control Planes to Data Foundations

For small-business leaders experimenting with agentic AI, the temptation is clear: more agents should mean more automation, faster results, and greater efficiency. But new research and enterprise case studies show that adding agents often reduces performance unless the underlying control and data layers are built first. Scaling agentic AI is increasingly defined by observability, identity governance, and data architecture rather than model upgrades.

Google and MIT tested 180 experiments across multiple model families and found that parallelized agent systems can improve performance by up to 81% over a single-agent baseline, but serialized tasks degrade by up to 70% when extra agents are added. Centralized multi-agent setups managed only 21 successful tasks per 1,000 tokens compared to 67 for single agents. The determining factor is not agent count but task structure: parallel, independent workflows benefit; sequential, state-dependent workflows suffer from coordination overhead, duplicated reasoning, and error propagation[^1].

This shifts the scaling question from “how many agents” to “can we govern each agent.” Once agents can plan and act across workflows, they behave like non-human identities with permissions, dependencies, and accountability requirements. Treating them as informal workflow tools rather than governed identities creates hidden access paths, weak rollback options, and audit gaps. For small businesses handling customer or financial data, that means applying the same seriousness to agent lifecycle management as privileged service accounts.

Enterprise adopters echo this priority. AWS’s agentic go-to-market transformation succeeded only after consolidating over 200 tools and 40 systems into 20 foundational data sets with a single taxonomy. The company found that growth was constrained not by missing AI features but by fragmented data and disconnected systems. Similarly, McKinsey’s analysis shows that 87% of surveyed organizations cite data quality and integration as the top barriers to scaling agentic AI, with human oversight and change management close behind[^2].

Architectural patterns reinforce the same lesson across industries. Successful multi-everything environments centralize identity, policy enforcement, observability, and cost attribution while keeping agent execution decentralized. Routing becomes dynamic, matching tasks to the right model or infrastructure tier in real time, and governance is embedded as a platform capability rather than bolted onto individual agents[^3].

The takeaway for small-business leaders is practical: before expanding agent use, map each workflow’s dependency structure, instrument runtime tracing, and classify each agent as a governed identity with a clear owner. Performance gains follow control, not complexity.

---

**Sources**

[^1]: Agentic AI scaling depends on observability before more agents — nhimg.org
[^2]: AWS McKinsey Group: Lessons in agentic AI — mckinsey.com
[^3]: Scaling agentic AI: Enterprise patterns without vendor lock-in — aws.amazon.com

This enables precise, data-driven strategy adjustments to improve results. [...] It’s no secret that content creation is one of the cornerstones of social media and one of the most complex, time-consuming parts of the marketing process. But today, there are AI-powered content creation tools (like Canva and Lumen5 along with generative AI tools like ChatGPT) that can simplify and optimize the end-to-end content lifecycle for us.

# AI in Social Media: How to Use it Wisely

January 17, 2025• 20MIN READ

Authors

[![Aishwarya Suresh](//images.ctfassets.net/ukazlt65o6hl/yZ4kDpd2gT7QkYgawhBuL/bb23fadc9e92321e5940af9c03f32351/Aishwarya_Headshot.jpeg?w=1080&q=50&fm=webp)

Aishwarya Suresh

Content Writer](/blog/author/aishwarya-suresh/)

AI in social media goes beyond predicting trends, personalizing content and automating posting. Today, AI enables creative thinking and storytelling in a way the average human mind cannot comprehend.

Have you ever just scrolled through your social feed and come across the coolest, most creative brand content? Believe it or not, all that eye-catching creativity is often powered by AI. Yes, you heard that right!

Today, smart brands are using artificial intelligence to revolutionize their social media, transforming how they connect with audiences. You’ve probably heard a lot about AI this, AI that — but when it comes to social media, AI isn’t just crunching numbers anymore. It’s unleashing creativity and telling compelling stories.

Take [Heinz’s “Draw Ketchup”](https://www.dandad.org/annual/2023/entry/professional/236760) campaign from 2023, for example. In partnership with branding agency *Rethink Ideas*, Heinz decided to launch the first-ever social media and print ad campaign with visuals generated entirely by the AI image generator DALL-E 2. Heinz asked the tool to generate the first picture it associated with the prompt “ketchup.” Astonishingly, the tool drew images that looked just like Heinz bottles! This happened not once, but every time it was fed ketchup-based prompts like “ketchup in outer space” and “ketchup scuba diving.”

## Ethical considerations of AI usage in social media

AI in social media offers numerous benefits, but it also raises important ethical questions. Here are some key ethical considerations to keep in mind:

**Privacy concerns:** Ever wonder how much of your personal data is being collected and used? AI algorithms analyze tons of user data to personalize content and ads. It's crucial that users are informed about these practices and have control over their data. No one likes feeling spied on!

**Bias and fairness:** AI can unintentionally perpetuate biases in the data it learns from. This means some groups might be unfairly treated or represented. To combat this, AI models need to be trained on diverse datasets and checked regularly for bias.

**Transparency:** Wouldn’t you like to know when you’re chatting with a bot or seeing AI-generated content? Transparency is key. Clear labeling and communication help maintain trust and prevent misunderstandings. After all, honesty is the best policy!

**Accountability:** If an AI system makes a bad call, who’s responsible? Brands must establish clear accountability for their AI tools' actions and decisions, ensuring there's always human oversight.

**Manipulation and misinformation:** AI can create persuasive content, which can be used to spread misinformation or propaganda. Social media platforms need robust policies and tools to detect and combat fake news.

**Job displacement:** Worried about AI taking over jobs? The automation of tasks by AI might lead to job displacement in many fields. While AI can enhance efficiency, it is essential to consider the social impact of reduced employment opportunities. Brands should think about the impact on their workforce and look into retraining and upskilling options. It’s all about adapting.

**Ethical use of data:** Using AI to enhance user experience is great, but it shouldn't exploit user data. Following ethical guidelines ensures data is used responsibly and for the benefit of users. Let’s play nice with data!

# 5 Ways To Use AI Social Media Tools And Where To Draw The Line

By[Jodie Cook](https://www.forbes.com/sites/jodiecook/ "https://www.forbes.com/sites/jodiecook/"),

Senior Contributor.

Edited by[Sophia Acevedo](https://www.forbes.com/sites/sophiaacevedo/ "https://www.forbes.com/sites/sophiaacevedo/"),

for [Small Business](https://www.forbes.com/sites/small-business/)

--:-- / --:--

This voice experience is generated by AI. [Learn more](https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesdigitalgroup/article/forbes-ai-audio-learn-more/).

This voice experience is generated by AI. [Learn more](https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesdigitalgroup/article/forbes-ai-audio-learn-more/).

## Summary

Social media AI tools can be useful for single owners and entrepreneurs by reducing costs and time. Many are also already using it. According to Constant Contact's Q1 2026 Small Business Now report, 54% of small businesses are currently using AI marketing tools. These tools streamline drafting, design, video, messaging and data analysis. However, the article stresses that while AI handles repetitive production, human judgment is indispensable for sensitive interactions, building trust and maintaining an authentic brand voice. Owners must strategically decide what to automate, reserving personal input for critical tasks like replying to complaints or crafting founder stories, and always posting manually for genuine engagement. Evaluate tools by hours saved, ensuring AI enhances efficiency without sacrificing the crucial human element.

TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. [Why Small Businesses Are Turning To AI For Social Media](#why-small-businesses-are-turning-to-ai-for-social-media-0)
2. [How AI Can Improve Your Social Media Marketing](#how-ai-can-improve-your-social-media-marketing-1)
3. [AI Social Media Tools Worth Considering](#ai-social-media-tools-worth-considering-2)
4. [Where Human Creativity Reigns On Social Media](#where-human-creativity-reigns-on-social-media-3)
5. [How To Build An AI-Powered Social Media Workflow](#how-to-build-an-ai-powered-social-media-workflow-4)
6. [How To Use AI Social Media Tools Like A Pro](#how-to-use-ai-social-media-tools-like-a-pro--5)
7. [Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)](#frequently-asked-questions-0)

Entrepreneur works online on laptop from home office. Social media AI tools can be used to help social media workflows and processes by helping build ideas, designing elements and analyzing data.

Getty

Social media AI tools can now handle work that used to need a full team. I sold my social media agency in 2021, before most of these tools existed. Back then, a single client post moved through a writer, a designer, a scheduler and an account manager. Today, one owner can produce the same output alone, in an afternoon, for less than the cost of one freelancer.

Business owners use social media AI tools every week to run their company with a leaner team than ever before. These tools cover drafting, design, video formats, messages and analysis.

## Why Small Businesses Are Turning To AI For Social Media

Small businesses turn to AI for social media because posting daily costs more time than most owners have. AI can speed up design and cut the hours lost to repetitive tasks.

Adoption has moved fast. According to Constant Contact's Q1 2026 [Small Business Now](https://www.constantcontact.com/blog/small-business-now-q1-2026-inflation-report/) report, which surveyed more than 1,500 owners across five countries, 54% of small businesses are currently using [AI marketing tools](https://www.forbes.com/sites/small-business/article/how-to-automate-small-business-marketing-with-ai-tools/) and another 27% plan to start this year.

I now run Coachvox, an AI company. Most of its marketing uses AI. We analyzed the chats that Jodie AI has to find out what our customers really want and the exact language they use. We coupled that with our brand guidelines to create landing pages, social graphics and email copy. We matched the revenue of my agency with a quarter of the people.

There is a cost to getting it wrong. Klaviyo [reported that 31%](https://www.klaviyo.com/solutions/ai/consumer-trust-in-ai) of people trust a brand less when marketing content is visibly AI-generated. Audiences forgive AI in the production process. They punish it when the output reads like a robot wrote it.

MORE FOR YOU

## How AI Can Improve Your Social Media Marketing

AI improves social media marketing most in tasks with volume and a clear right answer. Drafting, resizing, captioning, sorting messages and reading data all qualify. Anything resting on your judgment or your reputation stays with you. The same reasoning can be applied to other parts of the business process. For example, using [AI collaboration platforms](https://www.forbes.com/sites/small-business/article/ai-powered-collaboration-platforms/) still requires someone to oversee the tool.

Service businesses with an expert at the center gain the most, since coaches, consultants, agencies and trades all sell on trust and have a person in the spotlight. Good candidates for automation include turning one video into five clips, writing ten hook variations and pulling last month's numbers into a summary. Bad candidates include replying to a complaint, writing your founder story and posting anything about a customer without checking it first. The test is simple. If getting it wrong would cost you a client, do it yourself.

### 1. Speeding Up and Improving Ideas

AI closes the gap between having the idea and publishing it, particularly when that thought gets lost or it takes 40 minutes at a keyboard to become a post.

Before, your ideas would have sat unused in notebooks you forgot about. Now you can dictate an idea into AI as soon as you think of it, then the language model turns it into a draft. The cost is a few dollars a month against the hour a week spent staring at a blank screen.

Draft quality depends entirely on what goes in. Feed a model your past posts, your customer questions and your strongest opinions, and the output sounds like you. Feed it a one-line instruction and it sounds like everybody else. You have the tools. Now get good at using them.

### 2. Posting At Volume To Find Your Outliers

Growth on Instagram and TikTok comes down to a small number of posts. I analyzed multiple accounts that grew quickly and found the same pattern in each one. Two or three reels did the heavy lifting and everything else built the base underneath them.

Nobody can pick the outlier in advance, so you publish enough to find it, then make more of what worked. Business owners are using their personal Instagram accounts to generate leads for their companies. [Dorie Clark](https://www.instagram.com/dorieclark/), who has 304,000 Instagram followers, up from 24,000 a few months earlier, has been running a public Instagram experiment and inviting her audience to watch it unfold. [Nat Berman](https://www.instagram.com/realnatberman/) at 300,000 followers and [Rhys Morgan](https://www.instagram.com/thrivewithrhys/) at 235,000 both grew by testing formats and repeating the ones that performed.

AI makes that testing affordable, because producing 30 posts from scratch is a job that could take weeks, and producing 30 drafts with help is an afternoon.

### 3. Enhancing Design

Design used to be the bottleneck. A carousel meant a brief, a designer and two days of back and forth. Businesses without a designer used templates that looked like templates. AI design tools now generate on-brand graphics from a prompt and resize them for every platform.

Brand kits store fonts and colors so output stays consistent without anyone policing it. Background removal, resizing and translation take seconds. The financial saving reaches several hundred dollars a month against freelance design, and the trade off is true originality, since a prompt-generated graphic will share the hallmarks of other prompt-generated graphics. Photographs of you and your customers outperform anything generated, so use design tools for the frame and your photographs for the content.

### 4. Refining Answers To Comments And Messages

Replies drive reach on every platform. They also eat the day. A business posting daily can field dozens of comments and messages, most of them repeats of questions answered before.

Inbox tools sort messages into folders, add reminders and store saved replies, which turns an hour of scrolling into 15 minutes of decisions. AI can draft the answer to a repeated question and hold a first conversation with someone who lands on your website. Write the reply that closes a sale yourself. Anything sensitive or anything about money deserves your own words.

### 5. Reading Your Own Performance Data

Platform analytics show you numbers without telling you why. Working out which hook, length or format performed best means exporting data and comparing posts by hand, which almost nobody does.

AI turns that into a conversation. Browser-based assistants read what is on screen inside the session you are already signed into, so you can point one at your analytics page and ask what your best posts had in common, without connecting your social accounts to an outside vendor. Ask for patterns rather than summaries. The useful question is what the top ten posts share and what the bottom ten share.

## AI Social Media Tools Worth Considering

The market splits into four groups. Writing tools, design tools, video format tools and conversation tools. Prices run from free to around $100 a month, and the test is whether a tool removes a task you already do.

Judge each one on the hours it saves. Start on the free tier where one exists, use it for a month, then check whether you would notice its absence. A tool that saves 10 minutes a week of your VA’s time is not worth $50 a month. A tool that removes a weekly two-hour job pays for itself in the first fortnight.

### ChatGPT

ChatGPT drafts posts and captions, generates hook variations, builds content calendars and creates images. It suits any owner who wants one subscription covering ideas, drafts and visuals.

The free plan covers light use, and there are [more robust plans](https://chatgpt.com/pricing/) with monthly fees. Output quality drops when the prompt is thin, so it performs best when fed existing material rather than a blank instruction.

### Claude

Claude writes and analyzes data, and its Chrome extension operates inside the browser session the user has already signed into. It suits owners who want analysis and long-form drafting in the same place.

That browser access means it can read an analytics page without actually being logged-in as a third-party tool. Pricing runs from a free plan to other tiers that charge [monthly fees](https://claude.com/pricing?utm_source=google&utm_medium=paid_search_coder&utm_campaign=acq_code_us_q3&utm_content=pricing_text_v1&utm_term=nonbrand_claude%20code%20pricing&utm_source=google_brand&utm_campaign=%7Bcampaign%7D&utm_medium=cpc&utm_content=813552928539&utm_term=claude%20code%20pricing&targetid=kwd-2404422652503&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23948930353&gbraid=0AAAAAqwcL8lV73KmsutpONtQw3gALqjp3&gclid=CjwKCAjwhZDUBhBGEiwAbi5bjjLZwGJFUBXWStgelJTSa9gm7lxgl2YXLAfVYY7G9W0GpaSXcT3FlxoCwdcQAvD_BwE#team-&-enterprise), and the extension is limited to paid plans and to Chrome.

### Wispr Flow

Wispr Flow turns speech into text anywhere a keyboard works. A button press starts dictation and the tool cleans up the result, cutting filler and adding punctuation.

The free plan allows 2,000 words a week on desktop and it has [annual and monthly priced plans](https://wisprflow.ai/pricing). It suits anyone who thinks faster than they type. Talking for two minutes produces more usable material than typing for ten.

### Canva

Canva handles graphics and carousels, plus short video and scheduling. Brand kits keep colors and fonts consistent, and the AI features generate and edit images inside the same editor.

The free plan is generous and it has more plans with [monthly and yearly pricing](https://www.canva.com/pricing/). It suits businesses without a designer. The limitation is sameness, since millions of users work from the same template library.

### Format Finder

Format Finder, built by One Peak Creative, produces hooks, scripts and shot lists for a niche, edits the footage, then shows where viewers stop watching. It has multiple plans with [monthly or annual pricing](https://www.format.com/pricing-portfolio) and worth it for the growth you could unlock.

The argument for it is that somebody else has already run the tests. Instead of working out which short video formats hold attention from scratch, any business owner or marketing department can start from formats proven across other accounts and adapt them.

### Senja

A key goal of your social media should be to build trust with your future customers, and testimonials are a great way to do this. Senja collects customer testimonials through a form and turns them into shareable images and website widgets. Social proof posts require minimal writing, since the customer supplies the words.

The free plan covers up to 15 testimonials, and more robust [paid plans](https://senja.io/pricing). It suits any business with happy customers and no system for capturing what they say.

### Kondo

Kondo organizes LinkedIn messages with labels, folders, reminders, saved replies and keyboard shortcuts. It sorts sales pitches away from conversations worth having and stops follow-ups slipping.

Plans [can be billed](https://www.trykondo.com/pricing) monthly or billed annually, no free tier. It suits businesses generating inbound enquiries through LinkedIn. Below roughly 20 messages a week, the native inbox does the job.

## Where Human Creativity Reigns On Social Media

AI-generated emails, social media posts and websites follow a pattern. The first time you see one, you might think it looks impressive, then you realize everyone else’s work looks and sounds the same. But you'll be blind to this unless you analyze.

To win the game as a business owner, go back to basics. Scroll social media as a student. Understand what grabs attention, what creates intrigue and what makes people want to buy. Once you have this, not only can you put richer information into any AI tool, you need them less, because you have trained your intuition on what performs well.

Creative people are writing social media posts no AI could have written, finding camera angles that just look great and empathizing with their customers on a deep human level. Every business is grounded in human relationships. AI is no substitute for those.

## How To Build An AI-Powered Social Media Workflow

A social media workflow only works when there's a clear understanding of AI's role and how it should be used. Capture ideas by voice, refine or analyze with AI, design in a template, post by hand, then review the numbers weekly.

Post manually on Instagram, TikTok and LinkedIn. Posting by hand keeps you inside the app where the replies are, and replies drive reach. Review performance every Sunday and hunt for the outliers rather than the averages. Track one number per platform, whether that is saves, shares, profile visits or enquiries, then judge each subscription on whether that number moved after 90 days. If an AI tool fails to improve your social media workflow, cancel it.

## How To Use AI Social Media Tools Like A Pro

AI social media tools remove the production work that used to require a team. Use them to draft, design and analyze, then post by hand and reply as yourself. Volume finds the outliers, and outliers grow accounts. Start on free plans and pay only for the tools that give you back hours.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

An AI social media post generator turns a prompt, a topic or a rough note into a  caption or script. ChatGPT and Claude both do this, and Canva writes posts alongside the graphic. Format Finder specializes in short video, producing scripts and hooks for a named niche.

Feed any of them your own past posts before asking for something new. Output improves sharply when the model has your material to work from, and you can refine the posts further after the first draft.

An AI social media manager can draft, schedule, resize and summarize data, and it does all of that faster than a person but it cannot decide what your business stands for or handle an unhappy customer in public. Human managers hold the relationships, remember what happened last week, and know which post would embarrass you.

For daily management, Canva covers design and scheduling, Kondo organizes LinkedIn messages and Senja collects testimonials to post as social proof. Claude reads performance data straight from the browser.

Together those four cover design, messages, social proof and analysis for under $100 a month.

Format Finder writes short video scripts and flags the second viewers stop watching. Canva edits and captions clips, with a free tier that covers most of what a small business needs.

ChatGPT drafts scripts from a rough idea, and dictation tools like Wispr Flow capture that idea while it is still fresh. Film on a phone, then let the software do the polishing.

It even suggests different posting windows based on your goals, whether you’re aiming to increase engagement, build awareness, extend reach, or drive traffic.

Overall, Hootsuite brings planning, creation, publishing, and optimization into a single workflow, making it easier for teams to manage social media at scale.

**Price:** Hootsuite offers [a free 30-day trial](https://www.hootsuite.com/offer/blog)! After that, plans start at $199/month.

**Who it’s for:** Teams and enterprises managing multiple accounts.

![](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Best-Time-to-Post-Inpost-CTA.png)

Find out when your audience is online and optimize your posting schedule for maximum engagement. It’s so easy.

## **What are the best AI tools for content creation?**

The best AI tools for content creation are ChatGPT, Jasper, and Wordtune. These tools help marketers generate captions, brainstorm ideas, and repurpose content with ease.

Let’s take a closer look at each content creation tool.

### **2. ChatGPT**

ChatGPT is an AI writing assistant that helps marketers create both short- and long-form social media content.

It’s widely used for brainstorming ideas, drafting content, and repurposing existing material into new formats. Whether you’re building out an entire content calendar or need a quick first draft, ChatGPT can help you move with speed.

That said, it comes with a few limitations. For example, getting the right tone often takes very specific instructions, and its unedited outputs feel obviously AI-generated.

![Best AI tools for social media: ChatGPT](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-16.png)

*Source:* [*ChatGPT*](https://openai.com/blog/chatgpt)

For best results, treat ChatGPT as a starting point. Mold the output to match your brand voice, and fact-check key details, since it pulls information directly from the internet.

For all you content creators, check out our full list of [AI content creation tools](https://blog.hootsuite.com/ai-content-creation-tools/) that social media managers and creators love.

**Price:** Free basic plan; $20/month for faster image creation, expanded memory, and access to advanced reasoning models.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators and marketing teams.

### **3. Jasper**

Jasper is an AI copywriting tool built for teams looking to scale their content engine without losing their [brand voice](https://blog.hootsuite.com/brand-voice/) in the process.

Its standout feature is built-in tone guardrails, which help keep every piece of content consistent, even as output ramps up.

It also comes with a library of 100+ specialized AI agents, each designed to handle a different task in the content pipeline. For example, the landing page agent can create on-brand, conversion-ready landing pages, while the content translator agent adapts messaging for different languages.

![Best AI tools for social media: Jasper](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-26-620x341.png)

*Source:* [*Jasper*](https://www.jasper.ai/features/ai-assisted-content)

Jasper is especially useful for turning one idea into a full campaign. You can generate social media posts, repurpose long-form content into captions or scripts, and turn scattered ideas into a clear content plan.

**Price:** Plans start at $49 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Copywriters and marketing teams.

### **4. Wordtune**

[Wordtune](https://www.wordtune.com/) is an AI writing assistant designed to make your content easier to read. It rewrites your text to improve tone, flow, and phrasing without changing your original meaning.

It’s especially useful for long-form content like LinkedIn posts, where every word matters. You can adjust tone, tighten sentences, and clean up grammar in just a few clicks.

Wordtune can also summarize blog posts, documents, PDFs, and even YouTube videos, which is a handy shortcut for busy social media marketers.

![Best AI tools for social media: Wordtune](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-23-620x444.png)

*Source:* [*Wordtune*](https://www.wordtune.com/summarizer)

If you’re a writer, you’ll also want to see our full list of [copywriting AI tools](https://blog.hootsuite.com/ai-copywriting/).

**Price:** Free, paid subscriptions start at $6.99 a month.

**Who it’s for:** Long-form content writers and marketers.

## **What are the best AI tools for image editing and design?**

The best AI tools for image editing and design are Canva, Magic Studio, and Stockimg.ai. These tools help marketers create, edit, and generate high-quality visuals for social media.

Let’s take a closer look at the best tools for image editing and design:

### **5. Canva**

Canva is a user-friendly design platform that helps marketers create scroll-stopping visuals for social media.

If you’re already using Canva in your workflow, its AI features make it even more powerful. You can generate images by describing what you want, choosing a visual style (think: watercolor or film), and then dropping the results directly into your design.

![Best AI tools for social media: Canva](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-27-620x297.png)

*Source:* [*Canva*](https://www.canva.com/)

You can generate up to 50 images on the Free plan, or up to 500 images per user per month on Canva Pro.

**Price:** Free; paid plans start at $15 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators, small marketing teams, or solo social media marketers who need to generate a lot of graphics.

### **6. Magic Studio**

[Magic Studio](https://magicstudio.com/) is an AI tool that creates product photos with professional-looking backgrounds in a few different themes.

You can also remove unwanted objects from your images, which is useful for editing photos taken out in the real world.

On top of that, Magic Studio can generate images from text prompts and create profile photos, giving teams more flexibility in how they produce visual content.

Magic Studio is a strong option for brands and creators who want to improve the quality of their visuals without complex editing tools.

![Best AI tools for social media: Magic Studio](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image.jpeg)

*Source:* [*Magic Studio*](https://magicstudio.com/)

**Price:** Free with limitations. Paid plans start at $4.99 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Influencers, content creators, and e-commerce brands.

### **7. Stockimg.ai**

[Stockimg.ai](http://stockimg.ai/) is an AI image generation tool that helps marketers create custom visuals from simple text prompts.

Instead of scrolling endlessly through stock photo libraries, you can use this tool to generate images on demand in a variety of styles, including stock photos, illustrations, wallpapers, posters, logos, [art](https://blog.hootsuite.com/ai-art-prompts/), and more. This makes it easy to find visuals that match your content.

![Best AI tools for social media: Stockimg.ai](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-28-620x298.png)

*Source:* [*Stockimg.ai*](http://stockimg.ai/)

**Price:** Free, with paid plans starting at $19 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators, designers, and marketers.

## **What are the best AI tools for video?**

The best AI tools for video are Lumen5, Invideo, Munch, Peech, and Synthesia. These tools help teams turn ideas, scripts, or long-form content into engaging videos for social.

Let’s take a closer look at our top picks:

### **8. Lumen5**

[Lumen5](https://lumen5.com/) is an AI video creation tool that turns existing content into short, social-ready videos.

For example, say you have a blog post with tips for creating an engaging social media strategy. You can upload the blog post, and Lumen5 will generate a script and video to go with it. It’s an easy way to turn long-form content into short-form videos without heavy-duty editing software.

Lumen5 is a strong option for teams that want to extend the reach of their written content without investing in full video production.

![Best AI tools for social media: Lumen5](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-25-620x346.png)

*Source:* [*Lumen5*](https://lumen5.com/blog-to-video)

**Price:** Free, with paid plans starting at $19 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Content marketers and B2B marketers who want to turn long-form content into bite-size videos.

### **9. Invideo**

Invideo is an AI text-to-video generator that produces professional content based on prompts.

Want to turn your scripts into videos at the click of a button? Then [Invideo](https://invideo.io/) is for you.

Simply type in your video idea, and Invideo will generate a video with stock footage, voiceover, background music, and transitions — everything you need for a publish-ready video for TikTok, YouTube, or Instagram Reels.

Invideo has tons of video templates to get the creative ball rolling. You can create YouTube video intros and outros, videos for advertising on Facebook or Instagram with ad templates, and more.

**Pro tip 💡:** Use a long-form AI writing tool to generate a script, then feed that script to Invideo.

![Best AI tools for social media: Invideo](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-14.png)

*Source:* [*Invideo*](https://invideo.io/templates/social-media-videos/)

**Price:** Free, with paid plans starting at $15 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Marketers, content creators, and podcasters in need of video.

### **10. Munch**

[Munch](https://www.getmunch.com/) is an AI video repurposing platform that takes the most engaging parts of your long-form videos and turns them into short clips that are ready to share on social media.

![Best AI tools for social media: Munch](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-22.png)

*Source:* [*Munch*](https://www.getmunch.com/how-munch-works)

“This tool is fantastic for repurposing long-form videos into bite-sized content, each focusing on a specific talking point,” says [Bianca Garcia,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bianca-n-garcia/) Social Media Specialist at [Leadhub](https://www.leadhub.net/).

“It also generates AI subtitles, which has been a game-changer for [improving video accessibility](https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-video-tips/) and engagement,” she adds.

**Price:** Plans start at $49 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Social media marketing teams who want to ramp up their short-form video strategy.

### **11. Peech**

[Peech](https://www.peech-ai.com/) is a generative AI video editing software that can automatically transcribe, edit, and repurpose your video content.

Peech uses NLP technology to generate and scale high-quality video content. It can recognize your team’s faces and slap a title card onto the screen whenever they pop up. It can also automatically transcribe your video so you can repurpose it into captions or blogs.

Peech allows you to easily brand and edit video content without prior knowledge of video editing.

![Best AI tools for social media: Peech](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-18.png)

*Source:* [*Peech*](https://www.peech-ai.com/)

**Price:** Free with paid accounts starting at $49 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators, marketers, educators.

### **12. Synthesia**

[Synthesia](https://www.synthesia.io/) is an AI video tool that turns text into polished videos using AI avatars and voiceovers — no cameras, studios, or production team required.

It comes with customizable templates and branding options, so you can create explainer videos, promos, and social content that look professionally made.

It also supports multiple languages, meaning you can scale video content for a global audience without extra effort.

![Best AI tools for social media: Synthesia](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-28-620x298.png)

*Source:* [*Synthesia*](https://www.synthesia.io/)

**Price:** Free with paid plans starting at $22 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators, marketers, educators.

## **What are the best AI tools for voiceovers and audio content?**

The best AI tools for voiceovers and audio content are Riffusion and Murf.ai. These tools help creators generate custom audio, voiceovers, and music for videos.

Let’s take a closer look at our top picks:

### **13. Riffusion**

[Riffusion](https://www.riffusion.com/) is an AI music generator that creates original audio tracks based on your prompts.

For example, say you’re making a Reel but can’t find the right song to play in the background. Instead of scrolling through audio libraries, you can generate a song, instrumental, or vocal track that perfectly fits your video.

Riffusion does have its limitations. Common styles like “Bubblegum Pop” or “Jamaican Dancehall Vocals” tend to work best, while highly specific or unconventional requests may be less reliable.

![Best AI tools for social media: Riffusion](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-1.jpeg)

*Source:* [*Riffusion*](https://www.riffusion.com/)

**Price:** Free.

**Who it’s for:** Video content creators.

### **14. Murf.ai**

[Murf.ai](http://murf.ai) is an AI voice generator that creates realistic voiceovers for video and audio content.

It’s a practical (and budget-friendly) alternative to recording voiceovers yourself or hiring talent. You can generate audio in specific tones and moods, so your content sounds right — whether it’s a product launch, tutorial, or social video.

With 120+ voices across 20+ languages, it’s easy to create polished, on-brand audio at scale.

![Best AI tools for social media: Murf.ai](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-19.png)

*Source:* [*Murf.ai*](http://murf.ai/)

**Price:** Free. Paid plans start at $19 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Video creators, product marketers, educators, and content creators.

## **What are the best AI tools for productivity?**

The best AI tools for productivity are Fireflies.ai and Notion AI. These tools help teams capture ideas, automate note-taking, and organize content.

Here’s what makes them stand out:

### **15. Fireflies.ai**

[Fireflies.ai](http://fireflies.ai/) is an AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes, and summarizes conversations automatically.

For anyone who’s ever been part of a brainstorming meeting and found themselves typing at the speed of light to capture all of the ideas, you need to add [Fireflies.ai](http://fireflies.ai/) to your workflow.

It integrates with platforms like Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. It even generates searchable notes, so you can revisit discussions, extract key ideas, and turn meetings into actionable content.

![Best AI tools for social media: Fireflies.ai](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-20-620x490.png)

*Source:* [*Fireflies.ai*](http://fireflies.ai/)

For social media teams, it’s great at capturing brainstorming sessions and turning them into content ideas, briefs, or next steps without manual note-taking.

**Price:** Free, with paid plans starting at $10 per month.

**Who it’s for:** Social media and marketing teams.

### **16. Notion AI**

Notion AI is an AI assistant that helps teams plan, organize, and create content — all in one place.

Instead of jumping between tools, you can brainstorm ideas and create task lists and project trackers.

Because it’s built directly into Notion, it works seamlessly alongside your content calendar, briefs, and project docs, helping you organize all of your social media campaigns and assets.

![Best AI tools for social media: Notion AI](https://blog.hootsuite.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/image-24-620x390.png)

*Source:* [*Notion*](https://www.notion.com/product)

**Price:** Free plan available (includes Notion AI trial). Paid plans start at $20/month.

**Who it’s for:** Content creators and marketing teams.

## **5 free AI tools for social media**

### **1. Caption generator**

Stuck staring at a blank caption box? This free AI [caption generator](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/ai-caption-generator-social-media) has you covered.

Create platform-specific captions for Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, or X (Twitter) in seconds. Just choose your tone, add a quick prompt, include any keywords, and let the tool take it from there.

### **2. Hashtag generator**

Researching the best hashtags for every post is time-consuming. Let Hootsuite’s [free AI hashtag generator](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/hashtag-generator) do the work for you.

Automate the process by using the hashtag generator to come up with the right hashtags for every channel, whether you’re posting on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or LinkedIn.

### **3. YouTube video description generator**

You’ve done the heavy lifting of creating a video for YouTube, and now you need a video description. That’s where our [free YouTube video description generator](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/youtube-video-description-generator) comes in.

Descriptions aren’t just filler. They help viewers understand your content, drive traffic with links, and improve discoverability with the right keywords. The video description generator can be used for everything from Shorts to day-in-the-life vlogs.

### **4. Social media SEO tool**

Social media platforms are becoming search engines, which makes social SEO more important than ever.

This [free AI social media SEO tool](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/social-media-seo-tool) from Hootsuite helps you write captions that actually rank. Just choose your platform, tone, and target keywords, and it generates a search-optimized caption in seconds.

### **5. Sentiment analysis tool**

Social listening is a pillar of any social strategy, and [AI social listening tools](https://blog.hootsuite.com/ai-social-listening/) can help with that, too.

Hootsuite’s [free sentiment analysis tool](https://www.hootsuite.com/social-media-tools/sentiment-analysis-tool) can tell you within seconds how people feel about your brand. It can also help you understand the general feelings and attitudes toward competitor brands, trends, or specific creators and influencers.

## **4 tips for using AI social media tools from 4 social media managers**

Curious how marketers are making the most of social media AI tools? Here are a few use cases and tips directly from the experts.

### **1. Perform automated tasks**

AI tools can take a huge chunk of manual work off your plate.

For [Shanté Gorman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/shantegorman/), Founder and CEO of [Sugarpunch Marketing](https://sugarpunchmarketing.com/), AI tools like Butter help her automate tasks like recording and transcribing client calls.

**“We interview them on a call and then extract content that we can turn into short-form videos, carousel graphics, and text posts,”** says Gorman. **“This saves us at least 10 hours of time per client.”**

### **2. Develop content pillars**

AI tools can help you create content pillars by reviewing your existing content and surfacing common themes.

For example, you might use AI to review past blog posts and group them into core categories, like educational content, product updates, or customer stories.

[Cristy Stewart-Harfmann](https://www.linkedin.com/in/cristinamba/), a content creator and professor of digital marketing at Florida Atlantic University, recommends saving effective prompts to make this process more repeatable.

**“Once you find prompts that work well, save them for future use,”** she says. **“This can streamline your process and ensure consistency in content generation.”**

### **3. Continue training your tool**

One of the trickiest parts of AI-powered content creation is getting it to sound, well, human.

The best way to improve its output, according to [Bianca Garcia,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/bianca-n-garcia/) Social Media Specialist at [Leadhub](https://www.leadhub.net/), is pretty simple: “**Take the time to ‘train’ your AI tool.**”

To do this right, she recommends:

### **4. Be aware of platform rules**

Artificial intelligence is powerful, but it comes with strings attached. The rules for using AI are still evolving, and it’s on every marketer to stay compliant.

“I always stress to be cautious of what you plan to use from AI because there’s a gray area,” says [Megan Celestini](https://www.linkedin.com/in/meganwashington/), Social Media Specialist and Founder at [Queen Bee Social](https://queenbeesocial.net/).

“As social media professionals, it’s our job to eliminate the risk to the companies we work for and represent. If AI-generated content is not disclosed on certain social media channels, you could be violating the Terms of Service, and your posts can be taken down.”

If you plan to use AI for social content, Celestini recommends familiarizing yourself with each platform’s terms and conditions. YouTube, for example, asks you to disclose when you’re uploading [altered or synthetic content](https://blog.youtube/inside-youtube/our-approach-to-responsible-ai-innovation/) so it can label the video accordingly.

# AI in Social Media: 10 Powerful Ways to Grow Faster in 2026

[![Kalum](https://metricool.com/wp-content/litespeed/avatar/b2fee591788944830434bb57a08ebc3c.jpg?ver=1786441499)](https://metricool.com/author/kalumalleyne/ "Kalum")   Kalum   05 August 2026

[AI Marketing](https://metricool.com/ai-marketing/ "AI Marketing")

![](https://metricool.com/wp-content/uploads/feature-image-title-1781123086061.webp)

[Toggle](#)

Social media never slows down. One Minute you’re planning content, the next you’re chasing trends, answering comments, checking analytics, and wondering how it’s already Thursday. That’s why AI in social media has become such a powerful tool for marketers. From generating captions and repurposing content to scheduling posts and uncovering performance insights, AI helps you work faster and spend more time creating content.

The key is using AI to enhance your process, not replace it. A strong AI social media strategy combines automation with creativity so you can stay consistent, make better decisions, and focus on growing your brand. With tools like Metricool, turning ideas into results becomes a whole lot easier.

## How AI Is Changing Social Media Marketing

As you probably already know, social media marketing has become faster, more competitive, and more data-driven than ever before. Instead of spending hours brainstorming posts, manually publishing content, and digging through piles of analytics, marketers are using AI to simplify the behind-the-scenes work.

AI in social media helps teams create content more quickly across platforms, uncover valuable data points faster, and make smarter decisions backed by actual performance metrics. The result is less time spent managing tasks and more time spent building worthwhile strategies.

Here’s why social media managers are adopting AI in 2026:

* Growing number of social platforms
* Pressure to prove [ROI](https://metricool.com/roi-what-it-is/)
* Need for real-time optimization
* Increased publishing demands
* Rising expectations for faster content production
* Demand for more efficient workflows and automation

## 10 Practical Ways to Use AI in Social Media

AI is changing the way we use social media, but getting started doesn’t have to be complicated. You don’t need to overhaul your entire process to see results. Small changes can save time, improve performance, and make managing content a breeze. From generating social captions to boosting your SEO, here are ten practical ways to use AI in social media and build a better AI social media strategy in 2026.

### 1) Creating Captivating Social Media Captions

Coming up with fresh captions every day can be difficult, especially if writer’s block kicks in. AI helps speed up the process by generating platform-ready copy that aligns with your goals, giving you a strong starting point to personalize your content. Instead of staring at a blank screen, you can focus on refining ideas and publishing content.

### 2) Generating AI-Powered Social Media Posts

# 17 Best AI Tools for Social Media Content Creation (Tested for 2026)

[AI](/resources/ai/)

PublishedAug 3, 2026

I've tested dozens of AI social media content creation tools to find the ones worth adding to my workflow. These are the 17 that do everything from feeding my thinking to automating busywork.

Reading time
:   24 minute read

Author
:   [![](https://buffer.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=128,quality=75,format=auto/https://storage.ghost.io/c/6d/21/6d217297-aa70-41fe-b68d-e29e411dd3ed/content/images/2025/07/Headshots-Instagram-Post.png)Tamilore OladipoSr. Content Creator @ Buffer](/resources/author/tamilore/)

As a content writer at Buffer who's always deep in the latest AI tools, I've tested dozens to find the ones worth keeping. These are the 17 AI tools for social media content creation that do everything from feeding my thinking to automating the busywork, organised by where they come in my workflow.

I use AI to create social media content every single day, but probably not in the way you're thinking. Instead of typing in a prompt and then publishing, AI is woven into almost every stage of how I think, draft, design, and ship content. At Buffer, and on my own social media, I've grown to [nearly 30,000 followers](https://buffer.com/resources/how-to-increase-linkedin-followers/) across platforms.

But it took a while to get here. A year ago, my AI usage looked like most people's: open ChatGPT, ask it to write a caption, get something generic back, rewrite the whole thing anyway, and wonder what the point was. The problem was that I was using these tools one-dimensionally when the leverage was everywhere else.

Once I started using AI earlier in my process (to feed my thinking, not just my content calendar) and later (to automate the busywork eating my creative energy), the quality of my output changed. I was making better contnet with AI handling the friction.

## **Key takeaways**

* The best AI content creation tool depends on your bottleneck — ideas, drafting, production or distribution — not on a single "winner."
* Best for idea capture: Sublime (personal idea library) and Granola (turning talking into structured notes).
* Best for thinking and structure: Claude for sparring, ChatGPT for brainstorming that draws on your history.
* Best for visuals without a designer: Canva; for images with accurate text, Nano Banana Pro.
* Best for short-form video: CapCut; for editing video like a document, Descript.
* Best for automating the busywork: Zapier connects the rest of the stack with no code.
* You only need three to five tools — start where you lose the most time and add only when you outgrow what you have.

#### Jump to section

* [Tools to…](#tools-to)
* [Tools to feed your brain](#tools-to-feed-your-brain)

* [Tools to process ideas](#tools-to-process-ideas)

* [Poppy AI](#poppy-ai)

* [ChatGPT](#chatgpt)
* [Notion AI](#notion-ai)
* [Tools to draft, edit, and publish](#tools-to-draft-edit-and-publish)
* [Grammarly](#grammarly)
* [Buffer’s AI Assistant](#buffers-ai-assistant)
* [Tools to create visuals](#tools-to-create-visuals)
* [Canva](#canva)
* [Adobe Express and Firefly](#adobe-express-and-firefly)
